## 1. Discovery & Translational Science

* **[Commentary targets Jiangsu University DPP-IV targeted protein degrader](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/hold-minute)** — *Science*
  * A peer critique highlights a *J. Med. Chem.* paper by Wang et al. describing a cereblon-mediated bifunctional degrader of dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV) as a potential therapy for diabetes.
  * The molecule demonstrated a longer duration of action than standard pharmacological inhibition, though its clinical potential is limited by a lack of oral bioavailability.

* **[The cellular landscape of druggable RNA-binding proteins](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01531-2)** — *Nature Reviews Drug Discovery*
  * A perspective reviews the endogenous and disease-linked roles of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) in cellular RNA metabolism.
  * The authors outline therapeutic targeting strategies, emphasizing newly identified opportunities for targeting RBPs localized directly to the cell surface.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Gantenerumab and solanezumab reshape brain amyloid-β proteoforms in DIAD](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.22.26363432)** — *medRxiv*
  * A postmortem mass spectrometry analysis of brain tissue homogenates evaluated DIAD patients treated for ~4 years with Roche's gantenerumab or Eli Lilly's solanezumab.
  * Gantenerumab significantly reduced specific amyloid-β proteoforms in brain tissue, providing neuropathological context on clearance patterns that fluid and PET biomarkers cannot capture alone.

* **[CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies convert human regulatory T cells into cytotoxic effectors](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.23.26363285)** — *medRxiv*
  * Longitudinal bone marrow and peripheral blood single-cell RNA, ATAC, and TCR sequencing was conducted on multiple myeloma patients from the Phase 2 MajesTEC-5 trial of a CD3-engaging bispecific T-cell engager (BTCE).
  * BTCE therapy drove the expansion of cytotoxic CD8⁺ clones and converted FOXP3⁺ regulatory T cells (Tregs) into an AP-1-imprinted hybrid cytotoxic state characterized by *GZMA*, *GNLY*, and *NKG7* expression.

* **[APOE ε4 carrier status does not accelerate cognitive decline in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.27.26364131)** — *medRxiv*
  * A linear mixed-effects analysis modeled the placebo arm (n = 343; 686 ADAS-Cog14 observations) of the EXPEDITION 1 Phase 3 trial of solanezumab.
  * While the APOE ε4 allele is a major risk factor for developing Alzheimer's, carriers did not demonstrate a faster rate of cognitive decline over the 80-week follow-up period compared to non-carriers.

* **[Renal nutrient loss via SGLT2 inhibition promotes metabolic health but increases AKI vulnerability](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.24.754002)** — *bioRxiv*
  * A physiological study explored renal metabolite filtration and excretion pathways as a third component of energy balance alongside intake and expenditure.
  * The research demonstrates that while SGLT2 inhibition promotes metabolic benefits via nutrient excretion, this metabolic offloading increases susceptibility to acute kidney injury (AKI).

* **[Genetic variation, iron status, and FGF23 signaling converge in sickle cell disease renal calcium buffering](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.23.752598)** — *bioRxiv*
  * Single-cell multiomics in sickle cell disease (SCD) mouse models identified the distal convoluted tubule (DCT) as highly susceptible to calcium reabsorption dysfunction.
  * Dysfunction is driven by a reduction of calbindin 1 (CALB1), decreased Klotho-dependent FGF23 signaling, and intracellular calcium signaling; dietary iron restriction further worsened CALB1 and SLC8A1 levels, shifting DCT cells to inefficient glycolysis.

* **[Soft drugs: design principles and topical applications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01535-y)** — *Nature Reviews Drug Discovery*
  * A review outlines safety-focused "soft drug" design, where therapeutic agents undergo rapid and predictable metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect.
  * Highlights developmental candidates for topical applications, design guidelines, and metabolic stability optimization challenges.

* **[Somatic and germline telomere biology in sarcoma](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.26364135)** — *medRxiv*
  * An analysis of 11,792 sarcoma patients from AACR Project GENIE showed that telomerase activation (8.8%) and ALT-proxy ATRX/DAXX inactivation (8.0%) are mutually exclusive (OR = 0.52).
  * In MDM2-amplified dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS), telomerase activation is acquired through *TERT* amplification during dedifferentiation from well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDLPS).

* **[Ex-vivo 3D precision platform maps primary vs. metastatic tumor drug response heterogeneity](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.22.26357781)** — *medRxiv*
  * A study evaluated a 3D microtumor functional profiling platform preserving the native microenvironment in 6 split primary tumors and 7 matched primary-metastatic pairs (ovarian, colon, and breast cancer).
  * By measuring ex-vivo cytotoxic dose-response curves across four orders of magnitude, researchers quantified concordance correlation coefficients (ρc) to evaluate how tumor heterogeneity affects drug responses across sites.

* **[Dynamic ¹¹C-UCB-J PET identifies synaptic density and relative perfusion alterations in Parkinson’s disease](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.26364237)** — *medRxiv*
  * A study simultaneously assessed synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) density and relative perfusion (R₁) using dynamic ¹¹C-UCB-J PET in 30 Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and 30 controls.
  * Spatial covariance analysis of R₁ successfully derived the Parkinson's disease-related pattern (PDRP), which correlated with motor symptom severity when combined with nigral synaptic losses.

* **[Preclinical evaluation of a psychedelic for chemotherapy-induced neuropathy](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42811107/)** — *PubMed*
  * A preclinical study demonstrates that a psychedelic agent provides protective benefits against chemotherapy-induced nerve damage in vivo.

* **[Deep learning cardiac motion analysis reveals genetic and pathophysiologic determinants of HFpEF](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.26364208)** — *medRxiv*
  * Researchers integrated image segmentation and optical flow motion analysis on cine cardiac MRI from 83,569 UK Biobank participants to derive 32 myocardial and inner cavity velocity phenotypes.
  * The framework identified mid-diastolic velocities at a population scale, defining novel genetic architectures and candidate causal mediators for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

* **[Corticosteroid resistance evaluated in severe COPD exacerbations](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.24.26363953)** — *medRxiv*
  * A matched case-control study compared COPD patients hospitalized for exacerbations requiring ventilation to those with stable COPD.
  * Corticosteroid sensitivity was assessed ex vivo and in vivo during clinical quiescence (>45 days post-exacerbation), finding no evidence of intrinsic steroid resistance to support the ongoing clinical use of ultra-high steroid doses in these patients.

* **[Perivascular adipose tissue CTA density acts as a biomarker for carotid plaque inflammation](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.27.26364115)** — *medRxiv*
  * A study developed a pipeline to quantify perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) attenuation metrics (fat attenuation index, FAI) surrounding the common and internal carotid arteries from stroke cohort CT angiograms.
  * Carotid PVAT density was significantly higher in symptomatic culprit plaques than contralateral non-culprit or control segments, correlating directly with histological and proteomic markers of plaque inflammation and instability.

* **[Research ethics of chimeric mice with human cell-based cortex](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/30/xeno-mice-human-brains-cortex-research-ethics/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * An opinion piece explores the bioethical and cognitive implications of new research involving chimeric mice engineered with human cell-based cerebral cortex tissues.

* **[Biotech]** **[Landscape analysis of clinical PROTAC degraders](https://x.com/andrewpannu/status/2104951691317534858)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Analysis of 53 clinical-stage oncology PROTACs across 37 sponsors shows 85% are in Phase 1 or Phase 1/2 trials.
  * Most advanced assets target ER, AR, BTK, and KRAS G12D to address treatment resistance or target undruggable proteins. Chinese-origin companies account for roughly 40% of the sample and 75% of Phase 2 programs, while all 3 Phase 3 programs involve Big Pharma.

* **[10x Genomics launches Atera spatial biology platform](https://x.com/bradloncar/status/2104924147629322571)** — *X / Twitter*
  * First commercial shipments of the Atera spatial biology platform have begun, aimed at expanding research capabilities.

## 2. Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **[UniQure’s Huntington’s gene therapy AMT-130 fails to hit significance at 4 years](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/uniqure-huntingtons-four-year-data-gene-therapy-results/831611)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  * Four-year data from 12 high-dose participants of AMT-130, a one-time gene therapy designed to inhibit huntingtin protein production, showed a 44% slowing of disease progression on a cognitive/motor scale compared to an external control.
  * The difference failed to reach statistical significance, causing the company's market value to drop significantly.
  * A separate daily activity score showed a favorable 61% slowing of progression, which the company described as a positive treatment difference.

* **[Biotech]** **[Intravenous oncolytic adenovirus VCN-01 improves survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04705-y)** — *Nature Medicine*
  * The randomized Phase 2b VIRAGE trial evaluated VCN-01 (zabilugene almadenorepvec), a hyaluronidase-expressing oncolytic adenovirus, administered intravenously.
  * Patients with treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic cancer received VCN-01 in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) versus GnP alone.
  * The VCN-01 combination arm met its endpoints, demonstrating prolonged overall survival (OS) compared to standard chemotherapy alone.

* **[Psilocybin reduces egocentric bias in alcohol use disorder pilot trial](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.26.26364086)** — *medRxiv*
  * A randomized, controlled pilot study in recently detoxified patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD) and persistent depressive symptoms compared a 25 mg dose of psilocybin to a 1 mg active placebo.
  * The 25 mg cohort showed a significant reduction in egocentric bias and egocentric superiority in a visual perspective-taking task reaction time, correlated with subjective psychedelic intensity.

* **[tACS targets theta oscillations in methamphetamine use disorder](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42811072/)** — *PubMed*
  * A double-blind, randomized clinical trial evaluated transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) targeting theta oscillations to improve cognitive control in male patients with methamphetamine use disorder.

* **[Ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 evaluated for MCI biomarkers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42810842/)** — *PubMed*
  * A single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial (ACE-2020-EGb 761) investigated the long-term effect of EGb 761 on blood markers of inflammation and neurodegeneration in patients with mild cognitive impairment.

* **[Biotech]** **[Enliven Therapeutics reports 52-week data for EP-104GI](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105267123740147739)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Released 52-week data from the highest dose cohort of EP-104GI in the ongoing Phase 1b/2a RESOLVE trial for eosinophilic esophagitis.

## 3. Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Eli Lilly reports Phase 3b data for EBGLYSS](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105269261954662604)** — *X / Twitter*
  * New Phase 3b data demonstrate significant and rapid improvements in skin clearance, itch, pain, and patient satisfaction in patients with moderate-to-severe hand and foot atopic dermatitis.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Eli Lilly highlights Phase 3 retatrutide results](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105087314481291647)** — *X / Twitter*
  * In the TRIUMPH-2 trial of participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes, retatrutide (12 mg) delivered substantial weight loss, with patients losing an average of 49.6 lbs (20.8%) over 80 weeks, alongside significant A1C reductions.

* **[Biotech]** **[Ascletis and Sagimet present Phase 3 denifanstat data in acne](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105236700171542596)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Partner Ascletis presented positive full 52-week results from the Phase 3 open-label extension trial of denifanstat in acne at EADV 2026.

## 4. Regulatory & Approvals

* **[FDA charges Indian nationals in transnational counterfeit drug scheme](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-investigation-leads-charges-against-two-indian-nationals-involved-transnational-counterfeit-drug)** — *FDA*
  * The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Florida and the DOJ filed federal charges against Swapnadip Roy and Vicky Ramancha for conspiracy and smuggling.
  * The scheme involved infiltrating the American prescription drug supply chain with counterfeit medicines.

* **[FDA CDER issues M11 guidance for harmonized electronic clinical trial protocols](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/m11-clinical-electronic-structured-harmonised-protocol)** — *FDA*
  * The FDA released the M11 Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol guidance, template, and technical specification document.
  * The guidelines establish international standards for formatting, headers, common text, and standardized terminologies to facilitate electronic exchange and regulatory review of clinical trial protocols.

* **[FDA issues CGMP warning letters to global pharmaceutical and OTC manufacturers](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/veganicskn-limited-719883-02092026)** — *FDA*
  * Warning letters were issued to Australian finished pharmaceutical manufacturer VeganicSKN Limited and US-based developer Curia New York, Inc. for significant Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) deviations.
  * Additionally, active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) supplier Kellin Chemicals Co., Ltd. (China), and OTC manufacturers Stream2Sea, LLC and Bentley Laboratories LLC received warnings regarding manufacturing and quality control violations.

* **[Biotech]** **[CelCure Therapeutics launches REVTORPYK](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105267627325059387)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Announced that REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) is now commercially available in the U.S.

* **[Biotech]** **[DBV Technologies submits BLA for VIASKIN Peanut Patch](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105097821389045781)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA for the VIASKIN Peanut Patch targeted at children aged 4 to 7 years.

* **[Celmade issued FDA warning letter](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/celmade-735876-09142026)** — *FDA*
  * CDER issued a warning letter citing significant violations identified on the South Korean firm's websites (`celmade.co` and `celmade.net`).

* **[Fresenius Kabi AG issued FDA warning letter](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/fresenius-kabi-ag-733107-09222026)** — *FDA*
  * CDER issued a warning letter (Reference 320-26-129) following a facility inspection of the German company, addressed to CEO Pierluigi Antonelli.

## 5. Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **[AstraZeneca invests $2 billion in Summit Therapeutics to couple bispecific with ADCs](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/29/biotech-news-astrazeneca-invests-2-billion-in-summit-therapeautics/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * AstraZeneca committed $2 billion to collaborate with Summit Therapeutics.
  * The partnership aims to clinically test Summit's PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody ivonescimab in combination with AstraZeneca’s portfolio of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs).

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Novo Nordisk licenses preclinical weekly obesity pill from Hengrui for $2.6 billion](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-hengrui-oral-obesity-drug-deal/831607)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  * Novo Nordisk paid Hengrui Pharma $300 million upfront, with up to $2.3 billion in milestones, to license HRS-1596, an experimental, once-weekly oral weight loss candidate.
  * The deal secures Novo Nordisk's rights to the drug outside of China and Taiwan as the company moves to defend its metabolic franchise against competitors.
  * HRS-1596 is preclinical and has not yet entered human testing.

* **[Biotech]** **[Beam Therapeutics sues YolTech and Serapha over base editing trade secrets](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/beam-serapha-yoltech-base-editing-lawsuit/831663)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  * Beam filed a lawsuit in Massachusetts against Chinese biotech YolTech Therapeutics and its US partner Serapha Bio.
  * The suit alleges a former Beam scientist, Zi Jun "Emma" Wang, secretly founded YolTech while still employed at Beam and subsequently filed base editing patents based on Beam's proprietary trade secrets.
  * Serapha Bio has categorically denied the allegations and stated it will vigorously defend itself.

* **[Biotech]** **[PhRMA appoints former House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as CEO](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/29/eric-cantor-named-phrma-ceo/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) named former GOP House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as its new CEO.
  * The hire comes amid significant legislative and regulatory scrutiny of drug pricing and the pharmaceutical industry.

* **[Biotech]** **[Anthropic joins ARPA-H clinical AI initiative](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/29/anthropic-joins-arpa-h-clinical-ai-moonshot-health-tech/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * Anthropic has joined the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) clinical AI moonshot program.
  * The collaboration will leverage Anthropic's language models for healthcare-focused AI applications.

* **[Biotech]** **[Wave Life Sciences transitions siRNA program to GSK](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105265414603440604)** — *X / Twitter*
  * GSK selected an siRNA program from Wave Life Sciences to advance into further development, triggering a 12 million dollar upfront payment to Wave.

* **[Biotech]** **[Sagimet Biosciences prices public offering](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2105241739451629636)** — *X / Twitter*
  * Priced a 115 million dollar public offering of common stock at 10 dollars per share.

## 6. Public Health & Policy

* **[Open tracking data resolves MV Hondius Andes virus outbreak to Chilean reservoir zone](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.26364179)** — *medRxiv*
  * An open-data epidemiological investigation analyzed the 2026 Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak (11 cases, 3 deaths) aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship.
  * By integrating host *Oligoryzomys longicaudatus* rodent occurrences, serosurveys, and the index case's digital citizen-science travel logs, researchers traced the exposure to a known transmission focus in southern Chile and adjacent western Argentina, ruling out a suspected landfill in Tierra del Fuego.

* **[CDC and Pennsylvania conflict over measles-related death count](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/30/health-news-cdc-measles-death-count-still-lags-pennsylvania/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * Pennsylvania state health officials have documented four measles-related deaths this year, while the CDC's official national tally lists only two, highlighting communication and reporting lags.

* **[Biotech security advocates urge domestic capacity build to win US-China race](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/30/china-america-biotech-race-security/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * In an opinion piece, Gary Locke and Patrick McHenry argue that securing the US biological edge requires domestic capacity investment rather than solely relying on defensive trade and IP restrictions against China.

* **[Lawmakers challenge pending limits on imported medications](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/29/lawmakers-urge-trump-rethink-new-rule-that-could-restrict-imported-medicines/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * A bipartisan group of lawmakers is urging the Trump administration to reconsider a pending rule that could restrict Americans from importing prescription drugs from licensed pharmacies in Canada and overseas.

* **[Split opinions emerge over DEA scheduling of concentrated Kratom alkaloid 7-OH](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/30/dea-proposal-7-oh-kratom-schedule-1-drug/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * The emergence of highly concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products has renewed federal interest in regulating kratom.
  * Experts are split on whether to place 7-OH on Schedule I or adopt a standardized consumer protection regulatory model.

* **[Congressional delay stalls FDA Commissioner nominee Heidi Overton vote](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/29/heidi-overton-fda-commissioner-vote-midterms-health-care-policy/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  * Senate votes for key Department of Health and Human Services nominees, including FDA Commissioner nominee Heidi Overton, have been deferred until after the upcoming midterm elections.

* **[Real-world trial assesses reactogenicity of XBB.1.5 mRNA and protein-based vaccines](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42811742/)** — *PubMed*
  * The randomized BEEHIVE trial evaluated the real-world reactogenicity of the 2023–2024 XBB.1.5 mRNA and protein-based COVID-19 vaccines in healthy participants.

* **[Racial and ethnic disparities in buprenorphine and naloxone dispensing in Medicaid](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42811174/)** — *PubMed*
  * An analysis of Medicaid beneficiaries post-emergency department visit or hospitalization revealed significant racial and ethnic disparities in the prescribing and dispensing of buprenorphine and naloxone.

**Worth watching:** The commercial fallout from uniQure's AMT-130 Huntington’s disease readout, which wiped out $1 billion in market cap despite showing numerical slowing in progression, and the escalating intellectual property battle between Beam Therapeutics and YolTech over base-editing trade secrets.

    - [Rendez-vous le 01/10/26 !](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/W2G36KawZ4c) -- El Jj
        - The creator is launching a new "Mathctober" project, releasing daily short videos on random mathematical topics based on Inktober themes.
        - All project materials are created by hand without using artificial intelligence, representing two months of preparation.
        - The creator notes that the project was not fully completed at the time the announcement video was posted.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [Cet ingénieur a laissé l'IA gérer sa vie pendant 6 mois](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SeQXCpZhbjc) -- Underscore_
        - The video discusses an engineer who delegated the management of his daily life to AI agents for six months.
        - The content features a commercial partnership with Mammouth AI alongside a video with its co-founder.
        - The episode is hosted on set by Michaël de Marliave, Matthieu Lambda, and Maxime Gaudin, and is distributed across podcast platforms like Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and Deezer.
- Other
    - [Why Does the US Only Have Two Major Parties?: Crash Course US Government #2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HT8ikFog_pQ) -- CrashCourse
        - The video explores why the United States is bound to a two-party system and questions whether a viable third party could succeed.
        - The explanation attributes the dominance of two major parties to two primary categories: institutional systems and voter behavior.
        - The episode breaks down the subject through chapters on political parties, institutional explanations, and voter-side explanations.
